scenes.title: tidydiversity
scenes.subtitle: Version 0.3.0 · taxonomic, phylogenetic and functional diversity in one tidy workflow
scenes.say: Meet Tidy Diversity version zero point three: biodiversity analysis in R that is fair, fast, and ready to publish.

scenes.title: Unequal sampling, unfair comparisons
bullets: Raw species counts measure sampling effort
Fair comparisons need equal sample coverage
Taxonomic, phylogenetic and functional diversity on one scale
scenes.say: Sites are never sampled equally. Compare raw species counts, and you compare sampling effort, not nature.

scenes.title: Built to end package juggling
scenes.leftnote: Different formats for every project: hours of glue code
right: Checked against the references in 400+ tests
scenes.say: Every project used to mean juggling packages: i-next, vegan, betapart, F D, each with its own format, and glue code in between. Tidy Diversity was built to end that: one simple, consistent workflow that fits the tidyverse and tidymodels, checked against the reference packages in more than four hundred tests.

scenes.title: Tidy in, tidy out
scenes.say: One row per site and species goes in. A tidy table of Hill numbers comes out, for richness, Shannon and Simpson diversity, ready for d-plyr and g-g-plot.

scenes.title: Easy to learn, easy to teach
bullets: Predictable prefixes: div_, beta_, ord_, trait_, phylo_, model_
The same arguments everywhere: site, species, abundance
Learn one pattern, use every function
scenes.say: No more studying each package just to fit it into your workflow. Every function follows predictable prefixes and the same arguments, so once you learn one, you can use the rest. Easy to learn, and easy to teach.

scenes.title: Rarefaction and extrapolation by coverage
scenes.code:
curves <- div_rarefy(wet, q = c(0, 1, 2))
autoplot(curves, x = "coverage")
scenes.say: Rarefy and extrapolate to any sample coverage, and plot the curves in one line.

scenes.title: Taxonomic, phylogenetic and functional diversity
scenes.code:
div_rarefy(brazil, abundance = n, type = "PD", tree = tree)
div_rarefy(brazil, abundance = n, type = "FD", distance = dist)
scenes.say: Taxonomic, phylogenetic and functional diversity share one framework, shown here for two Brazilian rainforest assemblages.

scenes.title: State of the art, built in
bullets: Coverage-based Hill numbers for TD, PD and FD (Chao et al. 2014, 2019)
Beta diversity at equal coverage (Chao et al. 2023)
Max test for trait means, Welch PERMANOVA (Zeleny 2018; Hamidi et al. 2019)
Trait probability densities and gawdis distances (Carmona et al. 2019; de Bello et al. 2021)
scenes.say: It is built on the current state of the art: coverage-based Hill numbers, beta diversity at equal coverage, the max test, Welch PERMANOVA, and trait probability densities, straight from the recent literature.

scenes.title: Faster at every level, identical results
scenes.code:
bench::mark(iNEXT::iNEXT(wide, q = c(0, 1, 2)))
bench::mark(div_rarefy(brazil, abundance = n))
bench::mark(div_rarefy(brazil, abundance = n, type = "PD", tree = tree))
scenes.say: And it is fast. On real rainforest data, taxonomic rarefaction runs {td_w} times faster than i-next, and phylogenetic rarefaction about {pd_w} times faster than i-next 3 D, with identical results.

scenes.title: The bigger your data, the bigger the gain
scenes.say: The advantage grows with your data. At {scale_sw} species, Tidy Diversity is about {scale_w} times faster, thanks to compiled C plus plus kernels.

scenes.title: Preview: tidyvisor (in development)
scenes.code:
ord <- ord_fit(dune, method = "rda", formula = ~ Management + A1)
tidyvisor(ord)
scenes.say: Coming soon: Tidy Visor, in development. It explains your results in plain sentences, says when post hoc tests are needed, and writes the results sentence for your paper.

scenes.title: Full documentation online
scenes.say: Every function, tutorial and gallery example is on the package website, at tidy diversity dot in four metrix dot dev.

scenes.title: One family of packages
scenes.say: Tidy Diversity works with Tidy Mapper for spatial ecology. Tidy Visor and Tidy Epidemio are in development.

scenes.title: Get started
scenes.say: Install Tidy Diversity from GitHub today, and cite it with its Zenodo D O I.
